subtopics.title: Can the Bills Be Paid? — the Liquidity Ratios

questions.question: The current ratio for the year is:
options: 22 700 : 3 800 — about 6 : 1: six rand turning to cash for every rand knocking

questions.question: The acid-test ratio strips out inventories because:
options: Stock must first find a buyer, at full price, in time — it is the least cash-like current asset

questions.question: The guideline norms are:
options: Around 2 : 1 (current) and 1 : 1 (acid test) — held as GUIDES, not laws
There are no guidelines at Grade 10

questions.question: A very high current ratio can be criticised because:
options: It means the business is insolvent
Excess liquidity is idle money — cash sleeping instead of earning the mark-up or paying down the 12% loan

questions.question: The solvency ratio is:
The threshold that separates solvent from insolvent is:
options: 1 : 1 — below it, debts exceed assets and trading has legal consequences

questions.question: "Solvent but illiquid" describes:
options: Debts exceeding assets with plenty of cash
A business with no debts at all
Rich in equipment yet unable to pay Friday's wages — the whole game strong, the sprint failing
A failed acid test and a failed solvency test

questions.question: Solvency underpins the going concern assumption because:
options: Carrying assets at useful values presumes a future — a failing ratio questions the whole basis of the statements

subtopics.title: Return on Owner's Equity — Was It Worth It?

questions.question: Return on owner's equity uses the AVERAGE equity because:
options: The equity changed during the year — profit joining, drawings leaving — so the fair base is the mean of opening and closing
The formula sheet prints it that way without reason

questions.question: The calculation for the year is:
options: 7 900 / 21 950 × 100 ≈ 36% — profit over the average of 20 000 and 23 900

questions.question: The return gains meaning when compared against:
options: The safe alternative — a fixed deposit at around 8% — which the business must beat COMFORTABLY

questions.question: A business returning barely more than the bank's rate is a warning because:
options: The owner carries risk and does the work — a return equal to the safe rate leaves the risk unpaid

questions.question: The format habit for these answers is:
options: Ratios AS ratios (6 : 1) and percentages as percentages — format itself carries marks

questions.question: The classic error in return on equity is:
options: Using the UNAVERAGED equity — opening or closing alone — instead of the mean

questions.question: "Both directions score" in liquidity comments means:
options: Too LOW is dangerous (bills at risk) and too HIGH can be idle resources — the mature answer can argue either

questions.question: Every ratio is best learned as:
options: A formula to memorise despite the sheet
A DECISION quantified — the bank deciding to lend, the owner deciding to stay, the supplier deciding to give credit

questions.question: The month-end test asks:
options: Can what's coming in cover what's knocking at the door?
Did the year make a profit?

questions.question: "I can't pay the landlord in rice" is the household version of:
options: The acid test — re-asking the question with the hard-to-sell stock stripped out

questions.question: R15 000 sleeping under the mattress while the loan charges 12% shows:
options: Safety quietly becoming waste — enough should stay ready, the rest should work

questions.question: The whole-race count for the shop gives:
options: R38 900 owned against R15 000 owed — R2,60 for every rand owed: everyone could be paid

questions.question: The sprint and the whole race can disagree, as when:
options: A family owns a valuable house yet misses Friday's rent money — solvent, but illiquid

questions.question: Trading while insolvent means:
options: Spending money that already belongs to the creditors — which is why the bank checks this number first
Having no stock on the shelves

questions.question: The bank's order of questions is:
options: Could you pay AT ALL (solvency) before will you pay ON TIME (liquidity)

subtopics.title: Was It Worth the Owner's While?

questions.question: The owner's return computes as:
options: About 36% — R7 900 earned on an average stake of R21 950

questions.question: The bank's 8% and the shop's 36% differ in nature because:
options: The 8% is PROMISED; the 36% was EARNED — with labour, worry and risk, and no guarantee of repeating
The shop's figure includes the loan
Percentages from banks are calculated differently

questions.question: A shop returning 9% against a safe 8% deserves the advice:
options: RETHINK — a year of work and full risk for one extra rand per hundred leaves the risk unpaid

questions.question: This one ratio "joins the two statements" because:
options: The formula sheet lists it twice
Profit comes from the story page and the owner's stake from the photograph — one fraction answering a life decision
